newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Serb mercenaries terrorised Zaireans - residents.
newsitem.headline: Serb mercenaries terrorised Zaireans - residents.

text.p: Serb mercenaries cut a trail of terror through Kisangani, torturing and executing at will before fleeing as rebels captured Zaire's third largest city, residents said on Tuesday.
The mercenaries imprisoned and tortured dozens of young men accused of siding with the rebels and executed citizens at random for not possessing correct papers, eyewitnesses said.
Residents singled out a mercenary leader who called himself Colonel Dominic Yugo as notorious for shooting two evangelical pastors in cold blood while they held their Bibles and begged for mercy.

"Those were not mercenaries who came to save us. They were terrorists. They were carnivores," said Alpha Kangudi, 23, adding he saw Yugo shoot the two 10 days ago, 14 km (nine miles) outside the city.

The mercenaries, said by residents to number dozens, were among some 300 hired by President Mobutu Sese Seko to turn back the tide of rebel advances since October and organise an army counter-offensive from Kisangani in January that failed.
They abandoned the city last weekend after blowing up their headquarters at Kisangani's fortified and mined international airport 18 km (11 miles) outside town. Rebels say they left by helicopter.

"He (Yugo) was a tall, handsome guy, the type who could hit you while wearing a smile that said he would do you no harm," said Guy Mwanatambwe, 34, a businessman who said he had been arrested, jailed and tortured by the mercenaries.
"After Mobutu comes me. I am the second in command to Mobutu," Kangudi quoted Yugo as boasting.
Mwanatambwe said he saw them flee from the airport on Friday and he and fellow prisoners only survived because their captors were in too much of a hurry to leave to fulfill their threat of execution.
Locked in a cell at the airport they saw Yugo give the order to leave at 6 p.m. (1700 GMT), blowing up their camp and jumping into trucks during a rebel artillery barrage until eight p.m. (2100 GMT).
Mwanatambwe said he and four of his brothers were held at the airport for three weeks by the mercenaries, who tortured them with electric shocks and cut their faces with bayonets.
"It was Dominic himself who did the torturing because he spoke a little French asking 'Which one of you is the chief of the rebels,'" Mwanatambwe said.
He said the prisoners expected to die, having been told Mobutu had offered their captors $50,000 for every rebel killed.
Nineteen of 76 prisoners were taken away and executed at the airport, said Mwanatambwe, adding he only saw one death himself.
Business in Kisangani ground to a halt after the arrival of the mercenaries in the city on the Zaire river in January because residents were afraid to pass through checkpoints manned by them.

"The mercenaries sowed terror. They thought all the young men were rebels and had to be killed. Nobody could go out into town," said Benjamin Auta, medical director of the Roman Catholic Kabonda hospital.
Hundreds of defeated Zairean troops handed their guns over to the rebels on Monday in Kisangani. Some said they stayed behind when comrades left because they wanted a change in Zaire.
